own_solution.law: Coulomb's law and conservation of charge. Write the initial charges as +5Q and -Q. Initially F0 = 5kQ^2/d0^2. Contact gives each identical sphere charge +2Q, so F1 = F0(4/5)(d0/d1)^2 = 80(4/5)(30/60)^2 = 16 mN. An additional separation s gives F(s) = 16[60/(60+s)]^2 mN when s is expressed in centimetres.
assumptions: The identical conducting spheres share their conserved total charge equally on contact.
The stipulated point-charge model applies at both force measurements.
The remote rods do not disturb the field in the stated model.

notes: I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: the authors explicitly identify T162F and TCCA9 as numeral-free controls, rather than numerical minimal pairs. The solid-ball wording adds no dependency in that model.
